# Aanchal Malhotra | Oral Historian & Writer

> Official website and literary archive of Aanchal Malhotra (b. 1990), oral historian and writer based in New Delhi, India. She holds degrees in Traditional Printmaking and Art History, is the co-founder of the *Museum of Material Memory* (a crowdsourced digital archive of South Asian material culture and family heirlooms), and serves as Head of Oral History Projects at *South Asia Speaks*. Her books explore the 1947 Partition of India, material memory, generational inheritance, and South Asian history. She is represented by David Godwin Associates.

## Main Pages

- [Home](https://aanchalmalhotra.com/): Official homepage featuring Aanchal Malhotra's published books, forthcoming book spotlight (*A Handful of Home*), and author workspace overview.
- [About](https://aanchalmalhotra.com/about): Biography of Aanchal Malhotra, covering her background in printmaking and art history, published non-fiction and fiction works, literary awards (including the Council for Museum Anthropology Book Award and shortlistings for the British Academy Book Prize and Sahitya Akademi Yuva Puraskar), and archival initiatives.
- [Contact](https://aanchalmalhotra.com/contact): Verified contact details for South Asia interviews, publicity, and speaking invitations (Naiyya Singh, HarperCollins India), international rights and general enquiries (David Godwin, David Godwin Associates), and signed/personalised book orders (Bahrisons Booksellers, New Delhi).

## Books

- [Books](https://aanchalmalhotra.com/books): Overview of published and forthcoming non-fiction, fiction, and oral histories by Aanchal Malhotra.
- [A Handful of Home](https://aanchalmalhotra.com/books/a-handful-of-home): *The Partition of India in 100 Objects* (Forthcoming May 2027) — A children's book illustrated by Maryam Huq that introduces the history of the 1947 Partition through the stories of 100 everyday objects.
- [Bahrisons: Chronicle of a Bookshop](https://aanchalmalhotra.com/books/bahrisons-chronicle-of-a-bookshop): *An Homage to a Literary Institution* (2023) — The seventy-year history of New Delhi's iconic Bahrisons Booksellers in Khan Market, founded in 1953 by post-Partition refugee Balraj Bahri. Includes preface, archival photo gallery, excerpts, praise, and reviews.
- [The Book of Everlasting Things](https://aanchalmalhotra.com/books/the-book-of-everlasting-things): *A Novel* (2022) — Debut historical novel listed in NPR's Best Books of 2022, following perfumer Samir Vij and calligrapher Firdaus Khan across pre-Partition Lahore, the Western Front of the First World War, and Paris. Includes prologue, international editions, praise, reviews, and related media.
- [In the Language of Remembering](https://aanchalmalhotra.com/books/in-the-language-of-remembering): *The Inheritance of Partition* (2022) — Oral history tracing the cross-border, generational impact of the 1947 Partition across India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh. Includes prologue, editions, praise, reviews, and related media.
- [Remnants of a Separation](https://aanchalmalhotra.com/books/remnants-of-a-separation): *A History of Partition through Material Memory* (2017) — Non-fiction debut examining the 1947 Partition through the personal objects and heirlooms carried by refugees across the newly drawn border. Winner of the Council for Museum Anthropology Book Award (2022) and shortlisted for the British Academy Book Prize (2019).

## Reading Guides

- [Remnants of a Separation — Reading Guide](https://aanchalmalhotra.com/books/remnants-of-a-separation/reading-guide): Illustrated chapter-by-chapter archival companion and reading guide for *Remnants of a Separation: A History of Partition through Material Memory*, featuring photographs of the objects, people, and places documented in the book.

## Visual Art & Research

- [Visual Art & Research](https://aanchalmalhotra.com/visual-art-and-research): Index of visual art, traditional printmaking, and archival research projects.
- [The Book of Everlasting Things — Research (2017–2022)](https://aanchalmalhotra.com/visual-art-and-research/the-book-of-everlasting-things): Visual research archive documenting the making of the novel, including perfume distillation in Kannauj, calligraphy in Lahore, First World War archival records, smellscapes, and manuscript notes.
- [In Praise of Shadows — Traditional Printmaking (2014)](https://aanchalmalhotra.com/visual-art-and-research/in-praise-of-shadows): Limited edition copper intaglio print series on Arches paper created at Atelier de l'Île (Val-David), inspired by Jun'ichirō Tanizaki's 1933 essay on shadow, patina, and traditional aesthetics.

## Other Writing

- [Other Writing](https://aanchalmalhotra.com/other-writing): Selected essays, articles (published in *Wasafiri*, *Scroll*, *The Hindu*, *The Globe and Mail*, *Mint Lounge*, *The Times of India*, *Indian Express*, *Outlook*, and *Museum of Material Memory*), and anthology chapters (*The Book of Dog*, *Our Freedoms*, *India at 70*, *Departures in Critical Qualitative Research*, and *Looking Back: The 1947 Partition of India 70 Years On*).

## Press & Interviews

- [Press & Interviews](https://aanchalmalhotra.com/press-and-interviews): Curated interviews (*The Writing Desk*, *Hammock Magazine*, *Hindustan Times*), podcasts and video conversations (*The Himalayan Writing Retreat*, *Aga Khan Museum — This Being Human*), and literary features (*The Moment*, *New Lines Magazine*, *The Aleph Review*, *The Hindu*).
